retainedReference.title: Eanna
retainedReference.reason: No unique physical footprint or centerline with exact Wikidata identity has been resolved.

pictures.author: Marjon Verburg
pictures.observations: Entire700x525 ordinary site photograph inspected. Low excavated foreground, isolated eroded ochre/brown core with broad irregular horizontal shelves, sloping weathered sides and open flattened crown; a small marker stands at top. Named Eanna western-camera view establishes this constituent; no intact shrine is visible.

pictures.author: tobeytravels
pictures.observations: Entire1280x843 category-associated close photograph inspected. Exposed thin horizontal brick strata, broken terrace ledges, deeply eroded vertical/runoff grooves and irregular flat summit with a narrow marker. Used for surface/profile vocabulary, not surveyed dimensions or precise individual erosion slots; generic Uruk title alone does not establish geographic identity.

currentRoundInspection.scope: Surviving Eanna/Inanna ziggurat constituent of the named Eanna district: mapped irregular lower perimeter, eroded stepped brick core, broad broken shelves, runoff gullies and uneven open crown. No restored summit temple, intact ancient staircase or invented precinct-room grid. Other Eanna remains stay host terrain.
